label: input token o at original position 2 or 3
explanation: Fires only when the input token is o, essentially only during the original phase. On the dev split every o input at t=2 or t=3 activates (precision 1.0), at about 0.6-0.89 of max. The strongest examples are o at t=2 right after o (m o o). Weak activations (lowest quartile, often <0.1 of max) occur for o at t=1 (about 2.7k steps, mass share 0.6%), plus a few hundred at t=4 and a handful at t=5 or in the copy phase. Never fires at t=0, at the delimiter, at t>=6, or on any token other than o. Being the first o in the sequence raises the firing rate, but within t in {2,3} the feature fires regardless.

issues: Every claim I checked holds up. Test split: precision 1.000, recall 0.910, F1 0.953, mass recall 0.993, and misses found 0 false positives.

All 3,256 test misses are weak o activations outside t=2,3, holding 0.7% of activation mass. On the dev profile, t=1 has 2,734 active steps (0.6% of mass) and t=4 has 414, with values typically about 0.04 to 0.18 of max. The feature fires on only 17% of o inputs at t=1 and 2.9% at t=4, so widening the predicate to t in [1..4] gives recall 0.999 but drops precision to 0.57 and F1 to 0.73. These steps are a weak tail, not a gap the predicate should cover.

Copy-phase firing is negligible as claimed: 35 steps in dev, all at t=5 with recall_idx=2. The feature never fires at t=0, at the delimiter, at t>=6, or on any token other than o (all 36,124 active steps have in_tok=o).

Small wording issue: 'phase 0, t in [2,3]' is the same as orig_idx in {2,3}, so 'original position 2 or 3' is accurate. The claim that the strongest examples are o right after o was not tested directly. The top examples I sampled include o after non-o tokens at about 0.83 of max, so that claim is at most a weak trend.
